---
title: "Making a Quarto website easier to read"
subtitle: "Using CSS and SCSS with a consistent purpose"
---

## Why styling matters

For this site, I wanted visitors to find the main pages quickly and read the content without distractions. I used a warm background, dark green accents, and consistent headings. The navigation and page titles help visitors understand where they are.

## CSS controls individual elements

CSS changes how HTML elements look. A class selector lets me apply the same style wherever I need it. For example, `.demo-card` adds padding, a background, and a left border to the example below.

```css
.demo-card {
  padding: 1.5rem;
  border-left: 5px solid #225c51;
  background: #e9eee6;
  border-radius: 8px;
}
```

::: {.demo-card}
**A live CSS example**

This box uses the `.demo-card` class from `styles.css`. It gives a short takeaway a consistent visual treatment.
:::

In a QMD file, I apply it using a fenced div:

```markdown
::: {.demo-card}
Content goes here.
:::
```

## SCSS adjusts the theme

SCSS extends CSS with features such as variables and nesting. Quarto compiles the SCSS theme into CSS when the website renders. I used theme variables to set shared colors and fonts before the Bootstrap theme is compiled.

```scss
/*-- scss:defaults --*/
$primary: #225c51;
$body-bg: #faf9f5;
$body-color: #202e2b;
$headings-font-family: Georgia, serif;

/*-- scss:rules --*/
h2 { border-bottom-color: #cbd6ce; }
```

CSS works well for a specific component, while SCSS theme variables help keep the website consistent. Both are active in this project.

## Connecting the files

My `_quarto.yml` loads the base theme, my SCSS theme, and the CSS file:

```yaml
format:
  html:
    theme: [cosmo, theme.scss]
    css: styles.css
```

The same file defines the four navigation tabs. This avoids rebuilding the navigation on every page.

## Keeping the site usable

I included visible keyboard focus outlines, descriptive links, and a mobile media query that reduces the hero padding and photo area on small screens. Meaningful images need alternative text. I also kept the main information in text so color alone does not communicate meaning.
